newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Palestinians convicted over settler killings.
newsitem.headline: Palestinians convicted over settler killings.

text.p: A PLO court convicted three 20-year-old Palestinians on Wednesday for the killing of a Jewish settler and her young son in the West Bank last week.

The court sentenced two of the men, all members of the Popular Front for the Liberation of Palestine (PFLP), to life imprisonment at hard labour. The third was jailed for 15 years for driving the getaway car.

Israel had strongly pressed the Palestinian Authority to crack down on the PFLP, a radical Palestine Liberation Organisation faction which said it killed Etta Tzur and her 12-year-old son Ephraim at the Beit El settlement near Ramallah.

"The State Security Court established by decree of President Yasser Arafat sentenced the accused Abdel Nasser al-Qaisi and Ibrahim al-Qam to life with hard labour and Ibrahim Masaad to 15 years," the Palestinian Authority said in a statement.

Israeli security sources said Qaisi and Qam were arrested shortly after Tzur's car was ambused and sprayed with automatic fire. Masaad was seized on Wednesday along with assault rifles apparently used in the attack, they said.
The trial took place in Jericho in the former military headquarters of Israeli occupation authorites, witnesses said.
Asked if the Palestinian Authority would agree to extradite the three men to Israel, Palestinian preventative security chief Jabruil Rajoub told reporters: "It will never happen."
Jewish settlers laid the cornerstone of a new settlement in the West Bank on Wednesday in what they said was a response to the killings.
